levels.label: Nudge
levels.text: Write the regression tests before you touch the code, run them, and watch them fail. Then fix. Then check that a fix which only changed the obvious comparison would NOT be enough: is there a part for which it still fails?

levels.label: Approach
levels.text:
Your milestone 5 log told you two things about the limits: the operator, and the way they are computed. Section 4.4 says how to compare: at the gauge's resolution, 0.001 mm, never as raw floating-point numbers.

Work in whole thousandths of a millimetre (round each size, then compare whole numbers). Check the 4.5 and 4.6 rules in the same function: what happens to NaN, undefined, zero, negatives and very large readings?

levels.label: Near-solution
levels.text:
Round the reading, the nominal size and the tolerance to whole thousandths (Math.round(x * 1000)), then compare: at or above the upper limit is rework, at or below the lower limit is scrap, in between is pass. Before that, return recheck for anything that is not a finite number, zero or less, or more than twice the nominal size. Check the part type first, with Object.hasOwn.

Regression tests that fail on the old code: a shaft at 25.05, a sleeve at 19.08, a shim at 1.65, a spacer at 6.28 (scrap), and a NaN reading.

reveal.referenceBrief:
CONTEXT: classifyDefect in src/inspection/classifyDefect.js has bugs that tests/learner/classify.test.js found. The rules are in docs/tolerance-spec.md section 4 (4.4 says to compare at 0.001 mm).

TASK: First write tests/learner/regression.test.js: one test for each bug, named "regression: ...", each of which fails on the current code. Run them and show me that they fail. Then fix classifyDefect so that all of them pass.

CONSTRAINTS: Fix the cause, for every part: do not special-case a value or a part. Compare sizes as whole thousandths of a millimetre. Keep the name, arguments and return values. Do not edit parts.js or any test in tests/existing.

ACCEPTANCE: At least three regression tests, one of them for a part where changing only the comparison operator is not enough. npm test passes.

VERIFY: npm test. Then  npm run step -- 6.
reveal.approach:
The red-first sequence proves the fix: a test that fails on the old code and passes on the new one is evidence that the change did something. The half-fix check proves the fix reached the cause: if a test would pass after only changing the operator, the test is not guarding the whole bug.

Slide 216 names the trap: fixing the symptom (special-casing one boundary value) instead of the root cause (the comparison itself).
commonMistakes: Changing <= to < and stopping when the shaft test goes green.
Special-casing one value or one part.
Writing the regression tests after the fix, so that they were never red.
Regression tests that only use the shaft.
Fixing NaN but forgetting undefined, or forgetting exactly twice the nominal size.
Changing parts.js to make the numbers come out clean.
